answer.decision: Use staged canaries with automatic abort thresholds and backward-compatible schema changes.
answer.action: Begin with a 1% canary for at least 12 minutes, then expand through progressively larger regional and global stages with automated error-rate and p95-latency gates. Immediately disable the new routing path by feature flag and halt promotion if guardrails trigger; concurrently roll back the application if database read-pattern signals regress. Set thresholds early enough to prevent customer error rate from remaining above 1% for five minutes, retain additive schema fields during rollback, and complete healthy promotion to all traffic within one business day.
reasons: A 1% canary supplies statistically useful latency data in about 12 minutes, making staged production validation practical.
Prior routing regressions became visible through error rate or p95 latency within four minutes, supporting automatic detection and abort.
The routing feature flag provides a faster first response than the nine-minute global application rollback.
Additive schema fields are safely ignored by the old application, so rollback does not require a schema downgrade.
A global-at-once deployment exposes all customers before production-only failures can be contained.
Waiting six weeks for production-identical staging would miss the rollout objective and still would not reproduce third-party latency variance.
assumptions: Feature-flag propagation and automatic abort execution are fast enough to stop a detected routing-related breach before it persists for five minutes.
Monitoring can distinguish routing-path regressions from database read-pattern regressions and can trigger application rollback automatically or with an immediate on-call response.
The release can progress through enough stages within one business day while preserving the initial 12-minute observation window and appropriate later bake periods.
risks: A database read-pattern regression may require the nine-minute application rollback, so a threshold that triggers only after customer error rate exceeds 1% cannot guarantee the five-minute constraint.
Rare regional or scale-dependent failures may not appear in the 1% canary and could emerge during later stages.
Feature-flag propagation delays or monitoring gaps could prolong routing-related impact.
Aggressive promotion needed to finish within one business day may reduce observation time at later stages.

citations.claim: The previous three routing regressions were detectable in error rate or p95 latency within four minutes.
The additive schema is compatible with rollback because the old application safely ignores the new fields.
A 1% canary yields statistically useful latency signals in about 12 minutes.
A global application rollback takes nine minutes.
Production-identical staging would take six weeks and would still omit third-party latency variance.
The routing path can be disabled without redeployment, while database read-pattern changes require application rollback.
